name: 3 stars, with the owner's real 'make it shorter' edit in the history
source: real review 72263e68-8896-4b8f-a0e4-052422dfb2bb (Ember & Spice Grill); owner edit from 11 Oct 2026

review.text: Chicken tikka was tasty but the portion felt smaller than last time. Service was friendly enough.

fields.name: Ember & Spice Grill
fields.tone_notes: Warm, friendly and family-run. We talk to customers like regulars, even on their first visit. Short, upbeat sentences with a little East London charm. Use the customer's first name. Never pushy or salesy. Always say thank you. On bad reviews: apologise sincerely, never argue, and invite them back to make it right.
fields.halal_statement: All our meat is halal, certified by HMC.
fields.allergen_statement: Our kitchen handles nuts, sesame, gluten and dairy. Please tell our team about any allergy before you order.
recovery_offers: A free dessert on your next visit

checks.reason: Warm, short sentences, first name used, thanks given, sincere apology, invites them back. Matches the profile tone notes.
Names the Chicken Tikka and the portion concern from the review, and signs off as the family.
English reply to an English review. Plain words.
Opening 'Hi Kofi, thanks for the honest review' and closing 'get it right' differ from the supplied previous replies.
No em-dashes. One emoji, within the profile limit of 1 for review replies. No banned words.
Chicken Tikka, the smaller portion and the friendly team all trace to the review. Email, phone and sign-off match the profile.
The only numbers are the phone number, which matches the profile exactly.
No dates or times used.
'Kofi' matches 'Kofi A.'. 'Chicken Tikka' matches the menu.
No cause claimed.
No food, halal or allergen claims.
No offer made.
No targeting or wording based on personal traits.
Nothing offered in exchange for a review or for changing one.
Only details the reviewer wrote publicly. No order or booking details.
No financial, legal, medical or staffing advice.
Phone number and email are fine in a Google review reply.

Maker rules followed: same language, no argument, no invented facts, no staff named, no refund or money, no hashtags, emoji allowed, correct sign-off. Review does not trigger any escalation condition.
